headline: GOLD CRASHES TO $3,897, SILVER PIERCES $50 — December Fed Hike Now 83% Priced as Jobs Smash Forecast; Gold Down 26% from January ATH
snippet: Gold tumbled 3.1% to US$3,897/oz on Friday — its lowest level since early September — decisively breaking the $4,000 support cited by analysts as the key line in the sand. Silver was dragged below $50/oz for the first time in several months, amplifying gold's losses. Stronger-than-expected US jobs and manufacturing data deepened market bets on a December Fed rate hike, strengthening the dollar and driving Treasury yields higher. Gold has now fallen roughly 26% from its January 2026 all-time high above $5,300.

headline: ALAMOS Q3: ISLAND GOLD SHAFT SLIPS TO MID-2027 — AISC Hits $1,956/oz as 119K oz Meets Guidance; EPS Misses on Revenue of $510M
snippet: Alamos Gold (TSX/NYSE: AGI) produced 119,000 oz in Q3 2026 at all-in sustaining costs of US$1,956/oz — meeting quarterly guidance, but with adjusted EPS of $0.44 falling short of consensus on revenue of $510 million. A key negative: the Island Gold mine's production shaft has been delayed approximately one quarter to mid-2027, trimming near-term production growth. Full-year guidance of 510,000–560,000 oz remains intact, with heavier output weighted to Q4.

headline: NORTHWEST COPPER EXPANDS KWANIKA WESTERN ZONE AT DEPTH — 73.9m at 1.39% CuEq From 457m; 17 of 43 Holes Returned, System Open to Northwest
snippet: NorthWest Copper (TSXV: NWST) intersected 73.9 metres at 1.39% copper-equivalent (0.51% Cu, 0.79 g/t Au) from 457 metres depth in the latest holes from its 2026 Kwanika drill program in British Columbia, extending the Western Zone at depth. Assays are now back from 17 of 43 holes drilled in the 2026 program, with the Western Zone continuing to show broad, consistent copper-gold porphyry mineralisation that remains open to depth and to the northwest.

headline: NEW COPPER SKARN DISCOVERY IN MEXICO — Explorer Hits 88m at 1.6% CuEq in Broadest Intercept in Property History; New Structural Trend Opens
snippet: A TSXV-listed copper explorer reported an 88-metre intersection at 1.6% copper-equivalent — the longest and highest-grade result in the project's history — from a new skarn zone in Mexico, marking a step-out discovery that opens a fresh structural corridor across the property. The Margarita Skarn hole returned 14.37m at 1.1% CuEq from 624m alongside the headline intercept, suggesting the mineralised system extends well beyond the historic drill footprint. Mexico remains one of the top 10 copper-producing jurisdictions globally, with established smelter access and a history of large porphyry-skarn deposits in the Sierra Madre belt.

headline: NORTH ATLANTIC CRITICAL METALS: POKIOK PHASE I HITS ABOVE EXPECTATIONS — Antimony-Tungsten Drilling 70% Complete; New TSXV Junior Adjacent to North America's Largest Historical Sb Mine
source_name: Junior Mining Network / North Atlantic Critical Metals
snippet: North Atlantic Critical Metals (TSXV: NACM — began trading October 27) reported strong Phase I drilling progress at its Pokiok Project in New Brunswick, with 70% of the 5,000-metre program complete and results described as above expectations for antimony-tungsten-gold mineralisation adjacent to the Lake George deposit, historically North America's largest antimony mine. The release comes as US antimony stocks rallied 11% on October 27 amid growing US-China supply chain tension around the critical metal used in flame retardants, batteries and military applications. A total of 26 drill holes have been completed.

headline: MITHRIL SILVER-GOLD EXTENDS COPALQUIN-ZARAGOZA STRIKE TO 700M — High-Grade Ag-Au System Growing at Mexico's Target 4; Open Along Strike and at Depth
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Mithril Silver and Gold
snippet: Mithril Silver and Gold (TSXV: MSG) extended high-grade mineralisation at its Copalquin-Zaragoza structure to 700 metres of strike length at Target 4 in Durango State, Mexico — a continuation of the high-grade silver-gold epithermal system that has become the project's priority target. The extension results confirm a structural corridor running parallel to the Copalquin vein package, one of Mexico's historically prolific silver-gold districts. Mithril's Copalquin project covers 15,000 hectares in the same belt that hosted the historic Copalquin Ag-Au mine.

headline: OCTOBER CLOBBERS PRECIOUS METALS 7% — OANDA: Rate Cycle Is a Pause, Not a Structural Reset; $3,800 Is the Next Key Technical Floor
snippet: OANDA's October 2026 precious metals wrap shows gold down roughly 7% during the month — from $4,182 to the current $3,897 level — as the Fed's return to rate hikes crushes near-term sentiment. But OANDA argues the structural long-term bull case is intact: central bank buying continues at record pace, de-dollarisation trends are entrenched, and real rates remain historically low relative to inflation. OANDA identifies $3,800 as the critical technical support for the next directional signal, and notes that every prior Fed rate cycle since 2008 has eventually given way to further easing.

headline: 5 CANADIAN GOLD MINERS TO WATCH IN NOVEMBER — Island Gold, Detour Lake, Malartic Lead Screens; Energy Costs at $116/bbl Brent Squeeze AISC
snippet: Canadian Mining Report identifies five Canadian gold producers trading near multi-year discounts to spot NAV as Q3 reporting season wraps, with Agnico Eagle, Barrick, Kinross, IAMGOLD and Alamos all reporting within the October 28 to November 9 window. The piece notes that energy costs — Brent crude running at US$116/barrel — remain a live headwind for every mine on the list, keeping AISC elevated even as gold prices corrected. The analysts argue the best-positioned names are those with low-energy-intensity underground operations such as Island Gold and Detour Lake's truck-trolley-assisted haul.
